purpose: Classifies every currently modified/untracked repo path into ROUND-OWNED / INHERITED / AMBIGUOUS so Codex can stage this round's work by explicit pathspec only (never `add -A`, `add -u`, or `commit -a`) without sweeping in pre-round inherited dirt.

boundary.definition: The round-start snapshot, used as the cutoff between 'existed before this round' and 'touched during this round'.
boundary.boundaryTimestampSource: mtime of round-start-porcelain.txt itself, corroborated by R0/manifest.json's own worktreeFreeze.startPorcelainEntries: 161 and startPorcelainSha256 fields
boundary.currentSnapshot: `git status --porcelain` run at original classification time: 190 entries (169 ' M', 21 '??'; zero deletions, renames, or staged-index entries observed)
boundary.reconciliationNote: comm -23 (baseline-only paths) was empty: nothing present at round start has been reverted, cleaned, or removed since. Every one of the 161 baseline paths is still dirty.

steps: 1. Path-set diff (baseline vs current, path text only, ignoring status-code column) via `comm`. Paths absent from baseline = NEW-SINCE-ROUND-START (strong, unambiguous ROUND-OWNED signal since git had no record of them at all at round start). 29 such paths found.

2. For the 161 baseline paths still dirty (all of them -- 'common'), ran a repo-wide `find . -newer <baseline-file>` (Bash-tool loops that invoke `stat` per-path were silently broken by something in this harness -- a single top-level `find -newer` was used instead) and intersected the result against the common-path set on exact path text. This flags which pre-existing-dirty paths were ALSO written to after the boundary.

3. Applied different rules for TRACKED (' M') vs UNTRACKED ('??') paths that show post-boundary activity: a tracked file's working-tree diff accumulates ALL uncommitted changes since HEAD, so a pre-round-dirty tracked file touched again this round has a diff that BLENDS inherited content with round content and cannot be cleanly staged whole -> classified AMBIGUOUS, never ROUND-OWNED. An untracked file/dir has no such accumulation -- its current content is simply whatever was last written in full -- so post-boundary mtime on an untracked path is direct, unblended evidence of this round's authorship -> classified ROUND-OWNED, UNLESS live/ongoing bookkeeping state could not be ruled out.

4. Three untracked DIRECTORIES that were already dirty at round start needed special handling: git's porcelain collapses an untracked directory to a single line, hiding per-file churn inside it. Ran `find <dir> -newer <boundary>` directly against each (packages/core/scripts/quality-evidence/programs/, packages/core/test-artifacts/quality-evidence/, packages/showroom/src/app/probe/ds-reference/) to get true per-file before/after splits.

5. packages/showroom/src/app/probe/ds-reference/ resolved cleanly: ALL 21 files currently in the directory postdate the boundary -- nothing inherited remains to be swept in. Classified ROUND-OWNED as a directory pathspec.

6. Two documented project conventions were used to resolve specific tracked-file ties toward ROUND-OWNED despite pre-round dirt, because the convention guarantees a full mechanical overwrite rather than a hand-edited blend: (a) packages/core/src/foundation/tokens/css/facade/artifacts/**/index.css and packages/core/styles/*.css are declared build products of `pnpm -C packages/core build:vertical-css` -- hand-edits fail `lint:artifacts`; (b) roadmap/STATUS.md and roadmap/registry.json change ONLY via scripts/roadmap-status.mjs. The untracked packages/core/tenant-theme-canary-fixtures.json was similarly reclassified: its generator source siblings are untouched since the boundary, while only the generated .json output is touched.

7. Inside packages/core/test-artifacts/quality-evidence/wo-cra-23/, read R0/manifest.json directly. It self-describes as the SEALING document for the R0 baseline bundle, and by construction must be written AFTER round-start-porcelain.txt exists (it hashes it). Reclassified R0/manifest.json and its named companions (SUMMARY.json, SUMMARY.md, SHA256SUMS, receipts/incident-inherited-worktree-revert.json) from mtime-only AMBIGUOUS to INHERITED on this direct textual evidence. r1-canary-ownership-proposal.json (139KB) was NOT given the same treatment -- its content was not read, so it stays AMBIGUOUS.

8. packages/core/test-artifacts/quality-evidence/wo-cra-23/R1/ resolved cleanly the opposite way: all 76 files under it postdate the boundary with no exceptions. Classified ROUND-OWNED as a directory pathspec.
9. Where none of the above applied and a path had both before- and after-boundary evidence with no documented sanctioned mechanism, it was left AMBIGUOUS rather than guessed.

10. Self-caused reclassification: packages/core/src/foundation/tokens/css/runtime/engines/modern/skin/spinner.css was, at analysis time, in the pre-existing-dirty-but-untouched pool. This task then edited it (the authorized track-color rebase, see cohort-1-spinner-p48.json). That edit moved its mtime past the boundary and its diff now blends the inherited duration/comment hunk with this task's track-color hunk. Moved into AMBIGUOUS -- the one AMBIGUOUS entry with a fully-documented hunk-level breakdown available.
11. Cross-bucket overlap check: verified pairwise via `comm -12` between the three final path lists that no path appears in more than one bucket. All three comparisons returned empty.

12. OWNER-DIRECTED, added at regeneration: packages/showroom/cap-tmp.mjs was confirmed by the coordinator to be their own scratch capture script and must never be staged. Removed entirely from roundOwned; see excludedNeverStage. A filesystem-wide and dirty-set-wide search for sibling *-tmp.* / diag-tmp.* files under packages/showroom found none.

13. OWNER-DIRECTED, added at regeneration: packages/showroom/src/app/probe/whitelabel-torture/page.tsx (INHERITED, +100/-5772 per `git diff --stat`) and packages/showroom/src/app/probe/whitelabel-torture/scenes/ (was ROUND-OWNED, 8 new per-scene route files: forms, shell, all, primitives, dashboard, workflow, surfaces, data) are confirmed by the coordinator to be two halves of one refactor split across the inherited/round-owned boundary -- committing either alone would land a broken tree. scenes/ was removed from the plain roundOwned pathspec list (so a naive 'copy the array' staging workflow cannot grab it by accident) and both paths are now recorded together in knownCrossBucketCouplings as one held unit. page.tsx stays correctly listed in inherited (it already was -- inherited already means never-stage, so no bucket move was needed for it, only the explicit pairing record).
